description: Video-MME is the first comprehensive Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark for assessing MLLMs in video analysis. It consists of 900 manually curated videos spanning 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields, annotated with 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice QA pairs. The benchmark covers short, medium, and long videos (11 seconds to 1 hour) and integrates multi-modal inputs including video frames, subtitles, and audio.
name: Video-MME
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators had strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality was verified through a rigorous manual review process where each QA pair was examined by a different annotator. Additionally, text-only questions were provided to Gemini 1.5 Pro to filter out QA pairs answerable without video content. Statistical analysis shows that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, underscoring the robustness of the video content-based requirement. The distribution of answer options (A/B/C/D) follows a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring an unbiased evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning were recruited. Each annotator thoroughly viewed the entire video, then iteratively created three relevant questions, each accompanied by four candidate options, for a total of 2,700 QA pairs. Questions cover 12 distinct task types including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis. Each QA pair was designed to be closely tied to video content. A rigorous manual review process was conducted: each QA pair was examined by a different annotator to verify clarity of language, answerability with logically consistent options, and appropriateness of the correct answer. Text-only questions were provided to Gemini 1.5 Pro to filter out QA pairs answerable without video content.
rai:dataBiases: The distribution of answer options (A/B/C/D) follows a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring an unbiased evaluation. QA pairs that could be answered without video content were filtered out to prevent text-only bias. The benchmark was designed to prevent MLLMs from answering accurately without directly referencing the video.
rai:dataCollection: Videos were manually collected from YouTube across 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, Multilingual) with 30 fine-grained categories. Videos were collected with varying duration lengths: short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long (30-60 minutes). Corresponding meta-information including subtitles (if provided) and audios were also obtained. The resulting dataset consists of 900 videos, 744 with subtitles and all 900 with audios.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos sourced from YouTube across 6 visual domains and 30 fine-grained categories, along with their associated subtitles (if provided by the platform) and audio tracks. The dataset consists of 900 videos, 744 subtitles, and 900 audio files.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark reveals that all current MLLMs show a decline in performance as video duration increases, indicating limitations in processing longer video sequences. Open-source models are constrained by fixed numbers of input frames (e.g., 8 frames), resulting in excessively sparse information density for longer videos. Long context understanding remains a critical bottleneck for both single-modality and multi-modality models.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Video-MME is intended to advance the development of MLLMs capable of understanding sequential visual data, contributing to progress toward artificial general intelligence. The benchmark highlights limitations in current models for processing longer video sequences and multi-modal data, guiding future improvements in MLLM development.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating and benchmarking Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on video understanding tasks, including assessing capabilities in temporal reasoning, perception, and information synthesis across varying video durations and modalities (frames, subtitles, audio).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro was used during quality review to filter out QA pairs that could be answered solely based on textual questions without video content.
